normalized_issues.title: Path traversal protection has string-prefix bypass vulnerability and missing encoded/stream attack coverage

merged_from.title: Brittle screenshot path guards vulnerable to bypass under adversarial input
Screenshot canonical-path guard is vulnerable to root-prefix bypass and OS-dependent comparison bugs

normalized_issues.core_problem: The canonical-path guard uses a plain string StartsWith check, which is bypassable by sibling paths sharing a prefix (e.g. C:\shots2 starts with C:\shots). Additionally, URL-encoded traversal (%2e%2e), NTFS alternate data streams, and symlink following are not addressed. Case sensitivity differs across platforms.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 9 guard 3: 'reject with 403 if the resolved path does not start with Path.GetFullPath(ScreenshotRootPath)' — a plain StartsWith on a path without trailing separator allows sibling-directory bypass.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Append a trailing directory separator to the root before comparison, use OS-appropriate ordinal comparison, or use Path.GetRelativePath and reject results that are rooted or begin with '..'. Expand ScreenshotPathTraversalTests to cover encoded variants and sibling-prefix cases.

normalized_issues.title: IReadOnlyDhfRepository cannot distinguish 'session not found' from 'session with zero entries'

merged_from.title: IReadOnlyDhfRepository does not define how to distinguish an unknown session from an existing empty session
Omission of repository method for mandatory shallow validation status

normalized_issues.core_problem: ListEntriesAsync returning an empty list is indistinguishable from a valid session with zero entries. The mandatory GET / and GET /api/dhf/entries endpoints require 404 on unknown sessionId, but the interface contract provides no mechanism to detect non-existence. Additionally, the timeline page displays 'hash chain: valid (shallow)' but no shallow-validation method is defined on the interface.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SDR-06-003 lists only ListSessionsAsync, ListEntriesAsync, GetEntryDetailAsync, and ValidateChainAsync. Section 4.3 requires 404 for 'session not found'. Section 6 shows 'hash chain: valid (shallow)' in the mandatory timeline UI.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add SessionExistsAsync or GetSessionSummaryAsync to IReadOnlyDhfRepository, or define typed not-found semantics (e.g. SessionNotFoundException) for ListEntriesAsync. Also add a shallow-validation status method or clarify how the timeline obtains chain validity without a separate call.

normalized_issues.title: ValidateChainAsync contract is underspecified: no signature, no partial-result semantics on timeout, no isolation guarantee

merged_from.title: ValidateChainAsync contract is underspecified for the integrity endpoint requirements
Deep-validation timeout semantics have no mechanism for partial results
Cross-spec dictate on SPEC-04 isolation level creates untestable contract

normalized_issues.core_problem: The spec requires ValidateChainAsync to support shallow/deep modes, an 8-second CancellationToken hard timeout with partial results (entriesChecked, lastSequenceChecked, truncated=true), and repeatable-read snapshot isolation — but no method signature, DTO contract, or cancellation-to-partial-result mechanism is defined. A CancellationToken normally throws OperationCanceledException rather than returning partial state.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 5.3: 'Deep validation enforces an 8-second hard timeout via CancellationToken. If the timeout fires, the response is returned with results validated so far and truncated=true.' No validator or repository contract defines how progress is surfaced on cancellation.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Publish a concrete ValidateChainAsync signature including session id, mode enum, CancellationToken, and a result type that carries partial-result fields. Define explicitly how the validator accumulates and returns progress on cancellation (e.g. progress callback, incremental result object). Move isolation-level requirements into SPEC-04's interface definition.

normalized_issues.title: 503 vs 500 error mapping depends on RepositoryUnavailableException which may not exist in SPEC-04

merged_from.title: 503-vs-500 error mapping depends on an undefined repository exception contract
503 mapping depends on an undefined exception contract

normalized_issues.core_problem: The viewer's failure-mode table requires distinguishing RepositoryUnavailableException (→503) from all other exceptions (→500), but the spec hedges that SPEC-04 may not yet define this type and offers 'wraps NpgsqlException with IsTransient=true' as a fallback — which is not a stable, testable contract surface.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 14: 'RepositoryUnavailableException is defined in SPEC-04 ... If SPEC-04 does not yet define this type, it wraps NpgsqlException with IsTransient=true or TimeoutException.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Make RepositoryUnavailableException mandatory in SPEC-04 immediately. Remove the fallback wording. The viewer should catch only the concrete typed exception for 503 mapping.

normalized_issues.title: ACC-08 performance criterion uses manual demo validation on a specific laptop, not reproducibly testable in CI
normalized_issues.core_problem: ACC-08 requires < 1 second on the GE75 demo laptop measured manually. The CI regression guard uses a 3-second ceiling on unspecified hardware. The two thresholds are inconsistent and the primary criterion is not automatable.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 12: 'ACC-08 measurement methodology: Demo validation: Performed manually on the GE75 demo laptop. Threshold: < 1 second.' Section 11: 'TimelinePerformanceTests runs on every build with a 3-second ceiling.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define a reproducible automated test with a fixed dataset and a single threshold. If hardware variance is a concern, document a normalization approach or use a relative baseline rather than an absolute wall-clock number.

normalized_issues.title: Read-only DI enforcement is unverifiable without a defined isolated viewer composition root

merged_from.title: Read-only DI enforcement is not actually specified for an in-process shared host

normalized_issues.core_problem: The spec claims DI-based read-only enforcement via ViewerReadOnlyDiTests, but ViewerHost receives a repo instance directly from the orchestrator's DI setup. No separate viewer service provider is defined. In a shared in-process host, write-capable services registered in the orchestrator container remain accessible, and the test has no unambiguous isolated container to verify.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SDR-06-003: 'The viewer's DI container resolves only IReadOnlyDhfRepository.' Section 3: 'ViewerHost.Start(IReadOnlyDhfRepository repo, ViewerOptions options) is called from OrchestratorProgram.Main after DI setup.' No separate composition root is specified.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Define an isolated viewer WebApplication with its own IServiceProvider that registers only IReadOnlyDhfRepository. Specify the adapter pattern explicitly. ViewerReadOnlyDiTests should target this isolated provider.

normalized_issues.title: Feature tree field representation is contradictory between JSON example and field table

merged_from.title: Feature tree payload shape is inconsistent between the example and the field contract
Entry-detail API contract contradicts itself on feature-tree fields

normalized_issues.core_problem: The Section 5.2 JSON example shows featureTreeBefore as { "json": "..." } (a wrapper with a string), while the field table says the type is 'object' with notes 'SPEC-01 FeatureNode JSON'. These are two incompatible representations.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 5.2 example: '"featureTreeBefore": { "json": "..." }' vs field table: 'featureTreeBefore | object | yes | SPEC-01 FeatureNode JSON'.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Choose one canonical representation — either inline FeatureNode JSON object or a named string field — and align the example, field table, repository DTO, and tests to that shape.

normalized_issues.title: Entry detail read consistency is falsely assumed atomic; multi-table reads require explicit transaction scope

merged_from.title: Entry-detail consistency is falsely assumed rather than specified

normalized_issues.core_problem: Section 10 states 'Entry detail: Single-entry reads are atomic by nature,' but the entry-detail payload in Section 5.2 spans the entry row, tool calls, decorations, feature trees, and screenshot URLs — multiple tables. Concurrent writes can produce mixed-version payloads unless GetEntryDetailAsync explicitly uses a single consistent transaction.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 10: 'Entry detail: Single-entry reads are atomic by nature.' Section 5.2 payload includes toolCalls array, decorations array, featureTreeBefore/After, screenshotUrls — all from separate tables.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Require GetEntryDetailAsync to materialize all entry-detail data within a single read transaction/snapshot. Remove the 'atomic by nature' claim and replace with an explicit consistency guarantee.

normalized_issues.title: screenshotRootPath with %LOCALAPPDATA% token will fail startup without explicit environment variable expansion

merged_from.title: Configured screenshotRootPath will fail startup unless environment variables are explicitly expanded
Sample screenshotRootPath will fail startup unless environment variables are expanded

normalized_issues.core_problem: The documented appsettings.json example uses %LOCALAPPDATA%\BSVoiceCAD\screenshots. ASP.NET Core configuration binding does not expand Windows environment variable tokens. A literal Directory.Exists check on the unexpanded string will always fail, causing InvalidOperationException at startup when stretch endpoints are enabled.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 13 config example: '"screenshotRootPath": "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\BSVoiceCAD\\screenshots"'. Section 3 startup validation: 'throws InvalidOperationException at startup' if path does not exist.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Specify that ScreenshotRootPath is passed through Environment.ExpandEnvironmentVariables before validation, or derive the default from Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.LocalApplicationData) and require overrides to be absolute expanded paths. Update the config example accordingly.

normalized_issues.title: Viewer startup exception on invalid stretch config blocks entire orchestrator launch

merged_from.title: Viewer startup exception blocks entire orchestrator launch

normalized_issues.core_problem: ViewerHost.Start is called from OrchestratorProgram.Main. If EnableStretchEndpoints=true and ScreenshotRootPath is missing, the viewer throws InvalidOperationException, halting the entire orchestrator including the agent loop and modeling session. This contradicts the spec's framing of the viewer as a leaf module with no impact on core functionality.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 3: 'If EnableStretchEndpoints is true and ScreenshotRootPath is null or does not exist on disk, the viewer throws InvalidOperationException at startup.' Section 0: 'It never touches the agent loop.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Make stretch-config validation non-fatal: log a warning, disable stretch endpoints internally, and allow the orchestrator to start. Only throw on mandatory configuration failures (e.g. invalid port).

normalized_issues.title: Integrity validation ownership is contradictory: viewer vs. repository layer

merged_from.title: Integrity validation ownership is contradictory between viewer and repository layers

normalized_issues.core_problem: Section 5.3 says the endpoint 'Runs HashChainValidator.ValidateShallow or ValidateDeep' (viewer-layer logic). SDR-06-003 says 'All paths go through IReadOnlyDhfRepository.' Section 10 says ValidateChainAsync must be on IReadOnlyDhfRepository. These three statements are mutually inconsistent about where validation logic lives.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 5.3: 'Runs HashChainValidator.ValidateShallow (default) or ValidateDeep'. SDR-06-003: 'All paths go through IReadOnlyDhfRepository'. Section 10: 'SPEC-04's IReadOnlyDhfRepository.ValidateChainAsync must honor an IsolationLevel parameter.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Assign validation ownership to one layer. If the repository owns it, the viewer calls only IReadOnlyDhfRepository.ValidateChainAsync and HashChainValidator is an internal implementation detail of SPEC-04. Update all three sections to be consistent.

normalized_issues.title: Integrity validity semantics are defined for missing screenshots (warning, not failure)
normalized_issues.core_problem: Round 1 flagged this as undefined. Section 5.3 now defines the taxonomy explicitly: screenshot file missing = warning (valid unchanged), screenshot content mismatch = failure (valid=false). This issue appears resolved in v1.1.0.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 5.3 failure/warning taxonomy table: 'Screenshot file missing from disk (deep only) | warning | valid unchanged'.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: No action needed — resolved in current draft.

normalized_issues.title: Mandatory/stretch split is undermined by project scaffold and test inventory
normalized_issues.core_problem: The project scaffold lists stretch files (EntryDetailEndpoints.cs, IntegrityEndpoints.cs, ExportEndpoints.cs) alongside mandatory files without a clear build-time gate. The test inventory similarly mixes mandatory and stretch tests. A developer following the scaffold may implement stretch items believing them mandatory.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 1 project shape lists all files together with [Mandatory]/[Stretch] annotations only in comments. Section 11 test list mixes mandatory and stretch without a separate test project or conditional compilation symbol.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Either separate stretch files into a distinct folder/project gated by EnableStretchEndpoints, or add a build-time conditional (e.g. #if STRETCH or a separate .csproj) so the mandatory baseline is unambiguously isolated.

normalized_issues.title: Localhost-only threat model lacks pluggable auth boundary for post-hackathon deployment
normalized_issues.core_problem: SDR-06-002 documents localhost-only with no auth and defers multi-user auth to post-hackathon. No extension point or interface is defined for adding authentication, making the post-hackathon path a structural refactor rather than a configuration change.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: SDR-06-002: 'Post-hackathon: add authentication if multi-user.' No auth middleware hook or interface is specified.
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Add a note or stub (e.g. IViewerAuthPolicy) that can be a no-op for hackathon but provides a defined extension point for post-hackathon auth. Low priority for current scope.

normalized_issues.title: 3-second polling interval chosen without documented rationale or comparison to SSE
normalized_issues.core_problem: Section 7 specifies 3-second polling and explicitly rejects WebSocket but does not consider Server-Sent Events (SSE), which would provide lower latency without the complexity of a second WS endpoint.
normalized_issues.best_evidence: Section 7: 'Polls /api/dhf/sessions every 3 seconds... Specifically no WebSocket to the viewer... Polling is sufficient for hackathon scope.'
normalized_issues.recommended_fix: Low priority. If latency becomes a concern, SSE is a natural upgrade path. Document this as a known trade-off in SDR-06 or Section 15.
